questions.q: The state of Florida is a peninsula surrounded mostly by which body of water?
choices: Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico
questions.explanation: Florida is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean on the east and the Gulf of Mexico on the west.

questions.q: The Bamiyan Valley, where giant Buddha statues once stood carved into cliffs, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The Bamiyan Buddhas were destroyed in 2001 but had stood for over 1,500 years.

questions.q: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States. What does 'D.C.' stand for?
questions.explanation: D.C. stands for District of Columbia, named after Christopher Columbus.

questions.q: The Grand Canal, the world's longest artificial waterway, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: China's Grand Canal stretches over 1,100 miles and was begun over 2,000 years ago.

questions.q: London is the capital of the United Kingdom. Which famous river flows through it?
questions.explanation: The River Thames is about 215 miles long and has been important since Roman times.

questions.q: Louisiana is a US state known for its wetlands and swamps. Which city is its most famous?
questions.explanation: New Orleans is famous for jazz music, Mardi Gras, and Cajun food.

questions.q: Greece is a European country famous for ancient ruins. What is its capital?
questions.explanation: Athens is one of the oldest cities in the world and is called the birthplace of democracy.

questions.q: Baghdad is the capital of which Middle Eastern country?
questions.explanation: Iraq is located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers in a region once called Mesopotamia.

questions.q: Hershey, Pennsylvania is famous for producing which sweet treat?
questions.explanation: Hershey is called 'The Sweetest Place on Earth' and even has chocolate-themed street lamps.

questions.q: The Bund is a famous waterfront area in which Chinese city?
questions.explanation: The Bund features historic European-style buildings along the Huangpu River.

questions.q: Michigan is a US state shaped by which geographic feature?
questions.explanation: Michigan is split into two peninsulas and touches four of the five Great Lakes.

questions.q: The Treaty of Waitangi, signed in 1840, is the founding document of which country?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed between the British Crown and Maori chiefs.

questions.q: Naples is a large city in the southern part of which European country?
questions.explanation: Naples sits near Mount Vesuvius and is famous for being the birthplace of pizza.

questions.q: Gouda, a city in the Netherlands, is world-famous for producing which food?
questions.explanation: Gouda cheese has been made in the Netherlands since the Middle Ages.

questions.q: The North Pole is located in the middle of which ocean?
questions.explanation: Unlike the South Pole, which sits on land, the North Pole sits on floating sea ice.

questions.q: A 'favela' is a word for a hillside neighborhood or slum found in which country?
questions.explanation: Many favelas are built on steep hillsides in cities like Rio de Janeiro.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti plains are both found in which African country?
questions.explanation: Tanzania is also home to the island of Zanzibar.

questions.q: The Malay Peninsula is shared by Malaysia and which other country at its southern tip?
questions.explanation: Singapore is a tiny city-state at the very end of the Malay Peninsula.

questions.q: The Gulf of Mexico borders Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and which other US state?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is also bordered by Mexico and Cuba.

questions.q: The Arabian Peninsula, the world's largest peninsula, is home to Saudi Arabia and which other oil-rich country?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula also includes Yemen, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain.

questions.q: The 'Seven Summits' are the highest mountains on each continent. Which peak is the highest of all?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest in Asia is the tallest at about 29,032 feet.

questions.q: The Bermuda Triangle is a region in which ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously disappeared?
questions.explanation: The Bermuda Triangle lies between Miami, Bermuda, and Puerto Rico.

questions.q: The South Caucasus region includes Georgia, Armenia, and which third country?
questions.explanation: These three countries sit between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.

questions.q: Port Said is an Egyptian city located at the northern entrance of which famous waterway?
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

questions.q: Which of these is one of Canada's Maritime provinces, located on the Atlantic coast?
questions.explanation: The Maritime provinces are Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Prince Edward Island.

questions.q: The term 'Benelux' refers to Belgium, the Netherlands, and which third country?
questions.explanation: Benelux combines the first letters of Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg.

questions.q: Sherpas are a people famous for guiding climbers on Mount Everest. They live mainly in which country?
questions.explanation: Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa, was one of the first two people to summit Everest in 1953.

questions.q: The Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, is in which South American country?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Atacama have not received rain in recorded history.

questions.q: The Baltic countries are Estonia, Latvia, and which third nation?
questions.explanation: All three Baltic states border the Baltic Sea and joined the EU in 2004.

questions.q: The Gulf Stream is a warm ocean current that flows from the Gulf of Mexico toward which continent?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream helps keep Western Europe warmer than it would otherwise be.

questions.q: The Acropolis, an ancient hilltop citadel with the Parthenon temple, is in which city?
questions.explanation: The Parthenon was built around 447 BC in honor of the goddess Athena.

questions.q: The Mosquito Coast is a tropical region along the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and which other country?
questions.explanation: The name comes from the indigenous Miskito people, not from the insect.

questions.q: The Bay of Biscay lies between the northern coast of Spain and the western coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Biscay is known for its rough seas and strong storms.

questions.q: The Fertile Crescent, where farming first began, lies between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers in modern-day Iraq and which region?
choices: the Middle East and eastern Mediterranean
questions.explanation: The Fertile Crescent is often called the 'Cradle of Civilization.'

questions.q: The Tropics are the warm zone of Earth between which two imaginary lines?
choices: Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
questions.explanation: The tropics receive the most direct sunlight on Earth.

questions.q: After Kilimanjaro, what is the second-highest mountain in Africa?
questions.explanation: Mount Kenya stands at about 17,057 feet and is located in Kenya.

questions.q: Which is the busiest airport in the United States by number of passengers?
questions.explanation: Atlanta's airport has been the world's busiest for many years.

questions.q: Flanders is the Dutch-speaking northern region of which European country?
questions.explanation: Belgium is divided between Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia.

questions.q: The Han River flows through Seoul, the capital of which country?
questions.explanation: The Han River divides Seoul into northern and southern halves.

questions.q: The Rhone River flows through southeastern France and empties into which sea?
questions.explanation: The Rhone begins in Switzerland and flows through the French city of Lyon.

questions.q: Yuma, Arizona holds the record in the US for the most what per year?
questions.explanation: Yuma averages about 90% of possible sunshine hours, making it the sunniest city in the US.

questions.q: Sicily, Sardinia, and Corsica are large islands in which sea?
questions.explanation: Sicily belongs to Italy and is the largest island in the Mediterranean.

questions.q: The Great Pyramid and the Sphinx are famous ancient landmarks near Cairo in which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built about 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: The Humboldt Current is a cold ocean current that flows along the western coast of which continent?
questions.explanation: The Humboldt Current flows north along Peru and Chile, bringing cold water from Antarctica.

questions.q: The Gulf of Guinea is a large body of water off the coast of which part of Africa?
questions.explanation: Countries bordering the Gulf of Guinea include Nigeria, Ghana, and Cameroon.

questions.q: The state of Missouri is named after which major US river?
questions.explanation: The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States.

questions.q: Honshu is the largest and most populated island of which country?
questions.explanation: Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto are all located on Honshu.

questions.q: The Indian Ocean is bordered by Africa, Asia, and which other continent?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean in the world.

questions.q: The Arctic Ocean surrounds which pole?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the world's five oceans.

questions.q: The Balkans is a region of southeastern Europe. Which of these countries is NOT in the Balkans?
questions.explanation: Switzerland is in Central/Western Europe. Balkan countries include Serbia, Greece, Albania, and others.

questions.q: Andorra is a tiny country located high in the Pyrenees mountains between France and which country?
questions.explanation: Andorra is one of the smallest countries in Europe and is famous for skiing.

questions.q: Mount Rushmore, with four presidents' faces carved into rock, is located in which US state?
questions.explanation: The carving features Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln.

questions.q: Dublin is the capital of which European island country?
questions.explanation: Dublin sits on the River Liffey on Ireland's east coast.

questions.q: The Drake Passage is a stormy body of water between South America and which continent?
questions.explanation: The Drake Passage is one of the roughest stretches of water in the world.

questions.q: Wall Street, the center of American finance, is located in which US city?
questions.explanation: Wall Street is in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan.

questions.q: Arizona is home to the Grand Canyon and which famous desert?
questions.explanation: The Sonoran Desert covers much of Arizona and is home to the saguaro cactus.

questions.q: Victoria Falls, one of the world's largest waterfalls, is on the Zambezi River between Zambia and which country?
questions.explanation: Victoria Falls is about twice the height of Niagara Falls.

questions.q: The Atlas Mountains stretch across Morocco, Algeria, and which third North African country?
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains separate the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara Desert.

questions.q: Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, sits on the border of France and which country?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc stands at about 15,781 feet and its name means 'White Mountain.'

questions.q: Beijing is the capital of China. What does 'Beijing' mean in Chinese?
questions.explanation: Beijing has been China's capital for most of the last 800 years.

questions.q: The Windward Passage is a strait between Cuba and which other Caribbean country?
questions.explanation: The Windward Passage connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Caribbean Sea.

questions.q: London Heathrow is one of the world's busiest airports. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: Heathrow handles about 80 million passengers per year.

questions.q: The Han River flows through Seoul, dividing it into north and south. Seoul is the capital of which country?
questions.explanation: About half of South Korea's entire population lives in the Seoul area.

questions.q: The River Liffey flows through which European capital city?
questions.explanation: Dublin's name comes from 'Dubh Linn,' meaning 'black pool' in Irish.

questions.q: Guantanamo Bay is a US naval base located on which Caribbean island?
questions.explanation: The US has leased Guantanamo Bay from Cuba since 1903.

questions.q: The Museo Reina Sofia, home to Picasso's painting 'Guernica,' is in which European capital?
questions.explanation: The museum is named after Queen Sofia of Spain.

questions.q: Budapest is the capital of which Central European country?
questions.explanation: Budapest was formed by uniting the cities of Buda and Pest on opposite sides of the Danube River.

questions.q: The Baltic countries are Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. They all border which sea?
questions.explanation: All three countries were part of the Soviet Union until 1991.

questions.q: The Negev Desert covers more than half of which Middle Eastern country?
questions.explanation: The Negev is a triangular-shaped desert in southern Israel.

questions.q: Sumatra is one of the largest islands in the world. It belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Sumatra is the sixth-largest island in the world and is home to orangutans and tigers.

questions.q: Everglades National Park, a vast wetland home to alligators, is in which US state?
questions.explanation: The Everglades is sometimes called a 'river of grass.'

questions.q: Geysers are hot springs that shoot water into the air. Which country has the most active geysers?
questions.explanation: The English word 'geyser' comes from Geysir, a famous geyser in Iceland.

questions.q: Oahu is a Hawaiian island that is home to Honolulu and which famous military site?
questions.explanation: Pearl Harbor was attacked by Japan in 1941, bringing the US into World War II.

questions.q: Wisconsin is a Midwestern US state famous for producing which dairy product?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin is called 'America's Dairyland' and produces more cheese than any other state.

questions.q: The Tiber River flows through which European capital city?
questions.explanation: Legend says Rome was founded by Romulus and Remus on the banks of the Tiber.

questions.q: Tuscany is a region in central Italy famous for rolling hills, olive groves, and which city?
questions.explanation: Florence was the birthplace of the Renaissance and home to artists like Michelangelo.

questions.q: The Gulf of Tonkin lies off the coast of Vietnam and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Tonkin is part of the South China Sea.

questions.q: The Oresund Strait separates Denmark from which Scandinavian country?
questions.explanation: A famous bridge-tunnel connects Copenhagen, Denmark to Malmo, Sweden across the strait.

questions.q: South Carolina was one of the original 13 US colonies. Its largest city is which of these?
questions.explanation: Charleston is the largest city, while Columbia is the state capital.

questions.q: The Charles River separates Boston from Cambridge, home to Harvard University. In which state are both cities?
questions.explanation: The Charles River is about 80 miles long and is famous for rowing and sailing.

questions.q: Which is the largest city in Texas by population?
questions.explanation: Houston is the fourth-largest city in the entire United States.

questions.q: The Yucatan Peninsula, home to ancient Mayan ruins, is mainly in which country?
questions.explanation: The Yucatan is where an asteroid struck 66 million years ago, ending the age of dinosaurs.

questions.q: The Ural Mountains form a traditional boundary between Europe and which continent?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains run through Russia from north to south for about 1,500 miles.

questions.q: K2, the second-tallest mountain in the world, stands on the border between China and which country?
questions.explanation: K2 is in the Karakoram range and is considered harder to climb than Everest.

questions.q: The Orinoco River is the main river of which South American country?
questions.explanation: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers in South America at about 1,330 miles.

questions.q: Red Square, a famous plaza next to the Kremlin, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Red Square features St. Basil's Cathedral with its colorful onion-shaped domes.

questions.q: The Himalayas, including Mount Everest, form a border between India and which country to the north?
questions.explanation: The word 'Himalaya' means 'abode of snow' in Sanskrit.

questions.q: Land reclamation is the process of creating new land from the sea. Which city-state is famous for it?
questions.explanation: Singapore has increased its land area by about 25% through land reclamation.

questions.q: Yellowstone National Park is famous for Old Faithful and sits on top of which natural feature?
questions.explanation: The Yellowstone supervolcano last erupted about 640,000 years ago.

questions.q: British Columbia is a Canadian province on the Pacific coast. What is its largest city?
questions.explanation: Vancouver is one of the most diverse cities in Canada.

questions.q: How many Great Lakes are there on the US-Canada border?
questions.explanation: The five Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario.

questions.q: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand and is famous for its ornate temples. What are Thai Buddhist temples called?
questions.explanation: Bangkok has over 400 wats (temples), including the famous Wat Arun.

questions.q: The Himalayas are located in Asia and contain the world's highest peak. What is that peak called?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is about 29,032 feet tall and sits on the Nepal-China border.

questions.q: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya and has a national park within the city. What animals can be seen there?
questions.explanation: Nairobi National Park is the only wildlife park inside a major capital city.

questions.q: Which island's Mataveri International Airport is the world's most remote commercial airport?
questions.explanation: Easter Island (Rapa Nui) is over 2,000 miles from the nearest populated land.

questions.q: Rapa Nui, also called Isla de Pascua, is owned by which country?
questions.explanation: Easter Island is a Chilean territory in southeastern Polynesia.

questions.q: Which Pacific island owned by Chile is famous for its moai statues with large heads?
questions.explanation: The moai were carved by the Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500 CE.

questions.q: Thomas Cavendish was the first person to deliberately plan what type of global journey?
questions.explanation: Cavendish circumnavigated the globe in 1586-88, after Magellan's expedition.

questions.q: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, beginning and ending in Seville, was the first to complete what type of journey?
questions.explanation: Though Magellan died in the Philippines, his crew completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.

questions.q: Which river's source is Lake Tear of the Clouds on Mount Marcy in the Adirondacks?
questions.explanation: Lake Tear of the Clouds sits at 4,322 feet on New York's highest peak.

questions.q: The Tappan Zee is the widest point of which river that empties into New York Harbor?
questions.explanation: The Hudson River runs 315 miles from the Adirondacks to New York Harbor.

questions.q: Which island was transferred from the Republic of Genoa to France's King Louis XV in 1769?
questions.explanation: Corsica became French just one year before Napoleon was born there.

questions.q: Napoleon was born on which island, the largest of European France?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio, Corsica in 1769.

questions.q: Which mountain is over 33,000 feet tall when measured from its base on the ocean floor, making it the second-highest island peak on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea rises about 33,500 feet from the Pacific Ocean floor.

questions.q: What volcano is Hawaii's highest peak, standing 125 feet higher than neighboring Mauna Loa?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea stands 13,796 feet above sea level.

questions.q: Which city's Point State Park sits at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela Rivers, which form the Ohio River?
questions.explanation: Fort Duquesne was built by the French at this strategic river junction.

questions.q: What largest city of western Pennsylvania is known for its steel industry?
questions.explanation: Pittsburgh was once called the "Steel City" and produced much of America's steel.

questions.q: The Sentinelese people live on North Sentinel Island in which bay that also contains the Andaman Islands?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal is the world's largest bay by area.

questions.q: What is the world's largest bay by area, located between India and Myanmar?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal covers about 839,000 square miles.

questions.q: The Isthmus of Kra, separating the Andaman Sea from a namesake gulf, is the narrowest part of which country?
questions.explanation: The Isthmus of Kra is only 27 miles wide at its narrowest point.

questions.q: Which country, home to the island of Phuket, was previously known as Siam?
questions.explanation: Siam was renamed Thailand ("Land of the Free") in 1939.

questions.q: Which U.S. state, with its capital at Jackson, adopted a "Magnolia Flag" in 2021 and names a major American river?
questions.explanation: Mississippi replaced its Confederate-emblem flag with the Magnolia Flag in 2021.

questions.q: The Kolyma Highway, built by forced laborers, runs from Magadan to Yakutsk in which region?
questions.explanation: The Kolyma Highway is nicknamed the "Road of Bones" due to prisoner deaths during construction.

questions.q: The Ob, Yenisei, and Lena are the three major rivers of which remote Russian region?
questions.explanation: These three rivers are among the longest in the world and flow north into the Arctic Ocean.

questions.q: Which archipelago's island of La Gomera is known for its Silbo language that incorporates whistles?
questions.explanation: Silbo Gomero is a whistled form of Spanish used across the island's valleys.

questions.q: What Spanish archipelago off the African coast is named for dogs (Latin: canis), not birds?
questions.explanation: The name comes from Latin "Canariae Insulae" (Islands of Dogs).

questions.q: The Seven Mile Bridge is part of the Overseas Highway that terminates in which Florida city?
questions.explanation: The Overseas Highway runs 113 miles from the mainland to Key West.

questions.q: What city in the Florida Keys contains the southernmost point of the continental United States?
questions.explanation: Key West is about 90 miles from Cuba.

questions.q: The ancient Maya city of Tikal is located in which Central American country bordered by Belize and Mexico?
questions.explanation: Tikal was one of the most powerful Maya city-states, flourishing from 200-900 CE.

questions.q: Which Central American country displays a resplendent quetzal on its flag and is bordered to the east by Belize?
questions.explanation: The quetzal is Guatemala's national bird and its currency is also named after it.

questions.q: Much of the Star Wars series was filmed in which country's Tataouine Governorate, known for Berber cave dwellings?
questions.explanation: The planet Tatooine in Star Wars was named after the real Tunisian town.

questions.q: The ruins of Carthage and the eastern end of the Atlas Mountains are found in which North African country between Libya and Algeria?
questions.explanation: Carthage was an ancient Phoenician city-state near modern-day Tunis.

questions.q: The Mariana Trench contains what lowest point on Earth?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is about 36,000 feet below the ocean surface.

questions.q: What Middle Eastern country governed from Beirut is known for its Cedar Revolution?
questions.explanation: Lebanon's flag features a cedar tree, symbol of the country since ancient times.

questions.q: Which river forms the Vermont–New Hampshire boundary and flows past Hartford?
questions.explanation: The Connecticut River is the longest river in New England at 410 miles.

questions.q: Huascarán, the highest peak in the Tropics, is found in which South American country that also contains the Nazca Lines?
questions.explanation: Huascarán stands 22,205 feet in the Andes.

questions.q: Which country shares Lake Titicaca with Bolivia and contains the city of Lima?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca is the highest navigable lake in the world at 12,507 feet.

questions.q: The Peloponnese peninsula is technically made an island by the Corinth Canal in which country?
questions.explanation: The Corinth Canal was completed in 1893, cutting through 6.4 km of rock.

questions.q: The large island of Crete and Mount Olympus are found in which country governed from Athens?
questions.explanation: Crete is the largest Greek island and the fifth-largest in the Mediterranean.

questions.q: Lake Enriquillo, the lowest point of any oceanic island, is found in which Caribbean country?
questions.explanation: Lake Enriquillo sits about 150 feet below sea level.

questions.q: Punta Cana and Santo Domingo are located in which Caribbean country that occupies Hispaniola's eastern portion?
questions.explanation: The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.

questions.q: Which African country's Cap-Vert peninsula contains the island of Gorée, a former center of the slave trade?
questions.explanation: Gorée Island is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and memorial.

questions.q: What is Africa's westernmost country, with its capital at Dakar, that almost totally encases The Gambia?
questions.explanation: The Gambia is a narrow country that follows the Gambia River, surrounded by Senegal on three sides.

questions.q: The Skylon Tower overlooks which waterfalls whose three parts are called American, Horseshoe, and Bridal Veil?
questions.explanation: The Horseshoe Falls is the largest of the three, mostly on the Canadian side.

questions.q: What massive waterfalls on the border of New York and Ontario consist of the American, Horseshoe, and Bridal Veil falls?
questions.explanation: About 750,000 gallons of water flow over Niagara Falls every second.

questions.q: What capital of Arizona lies in the Valley of the Sun near the confluence of the Salt and Gila Rivers?
questions.explanation: Phoenix is the fifth-most populous city in the United States.

questions.q: Which city, Alaska's largest, was devastated by the 1964 Good Friday Earthquake and sits at the Cook Inlet?
questions.explanation: The 1964 earthquake was magnitude 9.2, the most powerful ever recorded in North America.

questions.q: The Gulf of Aden is the westernmost extent of which sea, connected to the Red Sea through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait?
questions.explanation: The Bab-el-Mandeb strait is only about 20 miles wide.

questions.q: What sea lies between India, Africa, and a namesake peninsula, containing the island of Socotra?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea is the northwestern part of the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: Bill Clinton was born in which U.S. state governed from Little Rock, home to Bentonville (Walmart's headquarters)?
questions.explanation: Bentonville, Arkansas is the global headquarters of Walmart, the world's largest company by revenue.

questions.q: The Arc de Triomphe, Eiffel Tower, and Pont Neuf are all found in which city on the River Seine?
questions.explanation: Paris is divided into 20 arrondissements (districts) spiraling outward from the center.
